new.title: Find it: a circuit of at most 44 AND/OR/NOT gates (fan-in at most two, every gate counted) computing the 3 by 3 times 3 by 3 Boolean matrix product
new.statement: ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (o : Fin 9 → ℕ), PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 44 ∧ ∀ x : Fin 18 → Bool, (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 0) false = (x 0 && x 9 || x 1 && x 12 || x 2 && x 15) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 1) false = (x 0 && x 10 || x 1 && x 13 || x 2 && x 16) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 2) false = (x 0 && x 11 || x 1 && x 14 || x 2 && x 17) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 3) false = (x 3 && x 9 || x 4 && x 12 || x 5 && x 15) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 4) false = (x 3 && x 10 || x 4 && x 13 || x 5 && x 16) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 5) false = (x 3 && x 11 || x 4 && x 14 || x 5 && x 17) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 6) false = (x 6 && x 9 || x 7 && x 12 || x 8 && x 15) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 7) false = (x 6 && x 10 || x 7 && x 13 || x 8 && x 16) ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (o 8) false = (x 6 && x 11 || x 7 && x 14 || x 8 && x 17)
new.unlocks: a circuit at 44 would be one gate under the schoolbook circuit we hold, with work shared between outputs; none found after a real search is evidence that 45 is least
new.context: The schoolbook circuit, nine ORs of three ANDs, has 45 gates (27 AND, 18 OR); an answer at 44 must share work between the nine outputs. Only the object is checked. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

new.sketch: Give the circuit as a gate list and the nine output wires; the proof is the gate kinds, the gate count and one evaluation over the 2^18 inputs. The schoolbook circuit, nine ORs of three ANDs, has 45 gates (27 AND, 18 OR), so an answer must share work between the nine outputs. Any search method is welcome; only the object is checked. We hold no circuit of AND and OR gates alone below 45 for it; say whether yours uses a NOT gate. A prover can use the lemma wire_of_expr in lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/ReplayColExpr.lean on main: one column comparison per output.

new.title: A fixed 32 by 32 bipartite graph given by its table: some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 128 gates is right whenever one row and one column are on
new.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 128 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 32 => (([0xf2bc7573, 0x59092a9d, 0xc443c8c2, 0x1d58483a, 0x1b7982bb, 0xa8882290, 0x74d0fd25, 0x00041402, 0x6879a8a5, 0xd65a6f1a, 0x7455fba3, 0x24508c1a, 0x3050a010, 0x68658ad5, 0x10a00735, 0x5e55690e, 0x6ab804a4, 0x00b01458, 0xf447af40, 0x00b07351, 0xa88c2290, 0x40d9d7bc, 0x40241486, 0x54058082, 0x6891afb9, 0x50ddf79e, 0x553080be, 0x28c180f8, 0x6ac8ae9e, 0xa6860e80, 0x20508c18, 0x10f01050] : List ℕ).getD u.val 0).testBit v.val) C
new.unlocks: a circuit under the count we hold for this graph; how low the count goes is what we want to learn
new.context: We hold 255 gates for this table: one AND of two ORs for each key, all ORed. Only the gate list is checked. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
new.sketch: Row u of the table, as a hex number, is entry u of the list in the statement; bit v is set when row u is joined to column v. The table comes from a keyed mixing rule of ours (k = 5). We hold 255 gates: for each key, the OR of its rows AND the OR of its columns, all ORed; sharing those ORs between keys brings ours to 225 (computed). Answer with a gate list; it is checked by one evaluation per promise input (1024). Any method. A prover can use represents_of_pcols in lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/PromiseCol.lean. At 128, four gates a side-vertex: truth unknown to us.

new.title: For every n at least 2, an n by n bipartite graph is represented with at most 2n more AND/OR gates of fan-in two than its complement
new.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), 2 ≤ n → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v => !A u v) s → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + 2 * n)
new.unlocks: if true, a graph and its complement cost the same on the promise up to a linear term, without NOT gates; a graph that breaks it is as welcome
new.context: Truth unknown to us. Tables at sides 3 and 4 agree (computed). The crown against the matching is the extreme case we know and it does not break it. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
new.sketch: Truth unknown. Tables at sides 3 and 4, computed, not checked: cost minus the complement's runs -2..2 and -4..4. One cell costs 1, its complement exactly 2n - 3 (every other line is read), so slope 2 is needed. Extreme case, crown against the matching (exactly 2n - 1): the claim asks crown <= 4n - 1; L-meta-18153 with L-meta-18183 give crown <= 3n + 4ceil(sqrt n) - 9 for n >= 4, below 4n - 1 at every n; n = 2, 3 cost 3 and 7. The checked transfer L-meta-18925 gives only twice the complement's plus about 6n.

new.title: Small cases only: on the one-a-side n by n promise, n >= 3, an AND/OR/NOT circuit of s gates gives an AND/OR one of at most s + 2n - 5 gates
new.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → C.size ≤ s → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 5))
new.unlocks: settles this statement on the record; whichever side is proved is kept
new.context: Truth unknown; our support is small cases only. A circuit with NOT gates right on the promise is turned into one without, paying at most 2n - 5 more gates. The exclusive-OR graph shows the slope cannot be lower: 4 gates with NOT against exactly 2n - 1 without, a gap of 2n - 5. At side 3 the bound is 1 above; a 3 by 3 graph costing 6 with NOT gates and 8 or more without would break it. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
